The discovery that atoms have a complex internal structure helped shape modern physics.
While developing a quantitative theory to explain atomic spectra, scientists discovered new laws of motion for microscopic particles: the laws of **quantum mechanics**.
prose.source_text: 原子复杂结构的发现是形成现代物理学的最重要的阶段. 这一阶段对物理学后来总的发展有深刻的影响. 在建立能够解释原子光谱的原子结构的数量理论的过程中，发现了微观粒子运动的新定律——**量子力学**定律.

prose.text:
The **Thomson model** was an early model of the distribution of electric charge inside an atom.
J. J. Thomson, the British physicist who discovered the electron, proposed that positive charge was spread uniformly throughout the atom, with electrons embedded in it.
In this model, the simplest atom, hydrogen, was a positively charged sphere with a radius of about $10^{-8}$ centimeters and one electron inside.
More complex atoms contained several electrons, like raisins scattered through a cake.
This was a historical model: later experiments on the distribution of positive charge showed that it did not correctly describe atomic structure.
prose.source_text: **汤姆生模型**  科学家们不是一下子就对原子结构有正确的概念的. 第一个原子模型是由发现电子的英国物理学家约·约·汤姆生提出的. 按照汤姆生的思想，原子的正电荷占据了原子的全部体积，并且在这体积中以恒定的密度分布着. 最简单的原子是氢原子，它是一个半径约为 $10^{-8}$ 厘米的带正电荷的球体，在其内部有一个电子. 一些比较复杂的原子的带正电荷的球体中有一些电子，这样，原子就象一个蛋糕，电子就象蛋糕里的葡萄干. 但是，汤姆生的原子模型和一些研究原子中正电荷分布状况的实验处于完全矛盾之中.

Ernest Rutherford's experiments were important in revealing atomic structure.
We will examine these experiments more closely to understand how they can test different models of an atom.
prose.source_text: 由英国伟大的物理学家厄奈斯特·卢瑟福进行的实验对原子结构的理解起了如此之大的作用，所以值得比在七年级物理课程中更详细地来讲述这些实验. 现在你们可以更好地理解这些实验的意义.
